messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: micro_era
parts:
Hey Mike!

I noticed something with the micro_era5 function. Although the arguments ask for dates in the format of d/m/Y, the output seems to be registering it as m/d/Y in the DOY column. So if I have the following

dstart <- "01/04/2018"
#for April 1, 2018
dfinish <- "31/08/2018"
#for August 31, 2018

Everything runs great, but in the DOY column in the metout table the first DOY is reported as 4 (for January 4). The first date is also reported as January 4 in the date vector (micro$dates).

It seems the problem is only with the dstart argument, since the last date is indeed on the same day as dend. Am I doing something wrong again?

Thank you!
Adam

messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: Re: micro_era
parts:
Follow up: it's possible this is a problem on my end, because I cleared everything and restarted R and I'm getting the right year now (of course it doesn't work for hours, then immediately fixes just as I report the problem....).

But I figured I'd leave this up just in case!

Adam
